best_for: Students, analysts and scientists who want Jupyter notebooks on their own computer without installing Python and JupyterLab by hand first.
description:
JupyterLab Desktop is the desktop app for JupyterLab, made by Project Jupyter and released as open source. It wraps the same JupyterLab you would run in a browser, but takes care of installing, starting and updating it, and it brings its own Python with numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib and ipywidgets already in place.

You can double-click an .ipynb file to open it, start a session in any folder, and come back to recent sessions from the welcome page. Each project folder keeps its own Python environment and window layout. The app can also connect to a JupyterLab server running elsewhere, including ones behind single sign-on, and the jlab command opens folders and notebooks from the terminal.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: The app is under the BSD 3-Clause license, with no account, plan or sign-in. You only sign in when a remote Jupyter server you connect to asks for it.

points.title: Use your own Python environments
points.text: Besides the bundled environment, the app finds conda, venv and pyenv environments on your computer and lets you pick one per project. You can also create new conda or venv environments from the app or with jlab env create. An environment needs the jupyterlab package to work with the app.

points.title: Only prebuilt extensions
points.text: JupyterLab extensions that install ready-made work fine. Source extensions, which need JupyterLab to rebuild itself, are not supported.

points.title: Windows: x64 only, installed machine-wide
points.text: There is one Windows installer, for x64 on Windows 10 and 11. It installs for the whole machine and supports silent installs. There is no Arm64 build.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 12 or later
points.text: Separate disk images are offered for Apple silicon and Intel Macs, both for macOS 12 Monterey and newer.

points.title: Linux builds exist, but not here
points.text: The project publishes a Snap, which it recommends, and .deb and .rpm packages for x64. This listing covers Windows and Mac only.

points.title: Uninstalling leaves the Python behind
points.text: Removing the app does not delete the bundled Python environment, settings or logs. The user guide lists the folders to delete by hand on each system.

points.title: Older builds for Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 12 versions. macOS lists only the current release, so an older Mac build has to come from the project's GitHub releases.
